text: Earth's surface magnetic field is roughly 25 to 65 microtesla
as_written: between about twenty-five and sixty-five microtesla
source: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, World Magnetic Model

text: The liquid outer core begins roughly 2,900 km below the surface
as_written: About twenty-nine hundred kilometres below your feet
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model, Dziewonski and Anderson 1981; USGS

text: The outer core is roughly 2,200 km thick
as_written: roughly twenty-two hundred kilometres thick
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model, Dziewonski and Anderson 1981

text: The inner core has a radius of about 1,200 km
as_written: about twelve hundred kilometres in radius
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model, Dziewonski and Anderson 1981

text: The inner core is about as hot as the Sun's surface
as_written: close to that of the surface of the Sun
source: Hirose, Labrosse and Hernlund, Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences, 2013; Alfè et al. 2002

text: Heat flow out of the core is on the order of 10 terawatts with a large uncertainty (roughly 5 to 15 TW)
as_written: somewhere around ten terawatts, though estimates differ by a factor of about three
source: Lay, Hernlund and Buffett, Nature Geoscience 2008, core-mantle boundary heat flow

text: Typical solar wind speed is about 250 to 750 km/s, with about 400 km/s typical
as_written: between about two hundred and fifty and seven hundred and fifty kilometres per second, and a typical value is around four hundred
source: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center

text: The sunward magnetopause sits near 10 Earth radii
as_written: it sits at about ten Earth radii
source: NASA Magnetospheric Multiscale mission; Shue et al. 1997 magnetopause model

text: Earth's mean radius is about 6,371 km
as_written: about sixty-three hundred and seventy kilometres
source: IAU 2015 nominal values; NASA Earth Fact Sheet

text: Ten Earth radii is about 64,000 km
as_written: around sixty-four thousand kilometres out
source: Arithmetic from the Earth radius of 6,371 km

text: Solar wind at 400 km/s covers 64,000 km in about 160 seconds
as_written: about a hundred and sixty seconds
source: Arithmetic from NASA typical solar wind speed and magnetopause distance

text: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth
as_written: about eight minutes to arrive
source: NASA Sun Fact Sheet

text: The atmosphere above a square metre weighs about ten tonnes, equivalent to roughly ten metres of water
as_written: about ten tonnes, which is equivalent to a column of water about ten metres deep
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet; standard atmospheric pressure of 101,325 Pa

text: Average natural background dose is about 2.4 millisieverts per year
as_written: about two point four millisieverts of radiation a year
source: UNSCEAR 2008 Report, Annex B

text: Cosmic rays contribute about 0.4 millisieverts per year to the average dose
as_written: roughly four-tenths of a millisievert
source: UNSCEAR 2008 Report, Annex B (0.39 mSv)

text: Magnetotactic bacteria were first described in the 1970s
as_written: first described in the nineteen seventies
source: Blakemore, Science 1975

text: Explorer 1 discovered the Van Allen belts in 1958
as_written: discovered in nineteen fifty-eight by Explorer One
source: NASA; James Van Allen, University of Iowa

text: The inner Van Allen belt spans about 1,000 to 6,000 km altitude
as_written: from about a thousand to six thousand kilometres above the surface
source: NASA Van Allen Probes mission

text: The outer Van Allen belt spans about 13,000 to 60,000 km altitude
as_written: from about thirteen thousand to sixty thousand kilometres
source: NASA Van Allen Probes mission

text: There are well over 10,000 active satellites
as_written: well over ten thousand active satellites
source: Union of Concerned Scientists Satellite Database; Jonathan McDowell's satellite catalog

text: GPS satellites orbit at about 20,200 km altitude
as_written: about twenty thousand two hundred kilometres
source: US Space Force / GPS.gov

text: The ISS orbits at about 400 km altitude
as_written: about four hundred kilometres
source: NASA International Space Station Facts

text: ISS crew receive about 80 millisieverts over a six-month stay
as_written: around eighty millisieverts over a six-month stay
source: NASA Human Research Program, radiation exposure on the ISS

text: 80 millisieverts is roughly 30 years of average natural background on the ground
as_written: roughly the dose you would collect from natural background on the ground over thirty years
source: Arithmetic from UNSCEAR 2.4 mSv per year

text: The March 1989 geomagnetic storm collapsed the Hydro-Québec grid in about 90 seconds
as_written: collapsed the Hydro-Québec grid in about ninety seconds
source: NASA Goddard; Hydro-Québec / NERC reports on the March 1989 storm

text: The 1989 blackout left six million people without power for about nine hours
as_written: Six million people lost power for around nine hours
source: NASA Goddard; NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center

text: The 1859 Carrington event disrupted telegraphs and pushed aurora to the Caribbean
as_written: set telegraph offices sparking and pushed the aurora down to the Caribbean
source: Carrington 1859, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society; Green and Boardsen 2006

text: The May 2024 storm was the strongest in about twenty years
as_written: the strongest geomagnetic storm in about twenty years
source: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center, May 2024 Gannon storm

text: Venus's induced magnetosphere boundary lies within a few hundred kilometres of the surface on the sunward side
as_written: within a few hundred kilometres of the surface on the sunward side
source: Pioneer Venus Orbiter ionopause measurements; Russell et al.

text: Mars's global magnetic field died roughly four billion years ago
as_written: roughly four billion years ago
source: Acuña et al., Science 1999, Mars Global Surveyor magnetometer; Lillis et al. 2008

text: Mars surface pressure is about 0.6 percent of Earth's
as_written: about six-tenths of one percent of Earth's
source: NASA Mars Fact Sheet

text: MAVEN measured solar wind stripping about 100 grams of gas per second from Mars
as_written: something like a hundred grams of gas every second
source: NASA MAVEN mission; Jakosky et al., Science 2015

text: Mars surface gravity is about a third of Earth's
as_written: about a third of Earth's surface gravity
source: NASA Mars Fact Sheet (3.71 m/s² versus 9.81 m/s²)

text: Venus surface pressure is about 92 times Earth's
as_written: about ninety-two times Earth's
source: NASA Venus Fact Sheet

text: Venus's hydrogen is enriched in deuterium by more than a hundred times relative to Earth
as_written: enriched in the heavy form, deuterium, by more than a hundred times compared with Earth
source: Donahue et al., Science 1982, Pioneer Venus Large Probe mass spectrometer

text: An intrinsic magnetic field does not simply protect a planet against atmospheric escape, and may in some conditions aid ion escape
as_written: A study published in Science Advances in twenty eighteen argued
source: Gunell et al., Science Advances 2018

text: Swarm launched in 2013
as_written: launched in twenty thirteen
source: European Space Agency, Swarm mission

text: The global field has weakened about 9 percent over the past 200 years
as_written: weakened by about nine percent over the past two hundred years
source: European Space Agency, Swarm mission

text: The South Atlantic Anomaly is a region of weak field where satellites suffer more radiation hits
as_written: a wide region where the field is especially weak, called the South Atlantic Anomaly
source: European Space Agency, Swarm mission; NASA Goddard

text: The last full reversal, Brunhes–Matuyama, was about 770,000 years ago
as_written: about seven hundred and seventy thousand years ago
source: IUGS ratification of the Chibanian stage GSSP, 2020; Suganuma et al.

text: The Cretaceous Normal Superchron lasted nearly 40 million years without a reversal
as_written: nearly forty million years without flipping once
source: Gradstein et al., The Geologic Time Scale 2012 (about 121 to 83 million years ago)

text: The Laschamp excursion occurred about 41,000 years ago
as_written: about forty-one thousand years ago
source: Cooper et al., Science 2021; Laj et al.

text: During Laschamp the field dropped to as low as about 5 percent of today's strength
as_written: as low as about five percent of today's strength
source: Laj et al. 2014; Cooper et al., Science 2021

text: The field was reversed for roughly 800 years during the Laschamp excursion
as_written: for roughly eight hundred years, pointed the wrong way
source: Cooper et al., Science 2021, Adams Event kauri tree-ring record

text: Cooper et al. used kauri trees preserved in a New Zealand bog, some more than 40,000 years old
as_written: some more than forty thousand years old
source: Cooper et al., Science 2021

text: Cooper et al. proposed links between the Laschamp excursion and climate shifts and extinctions, a proposal that is disputed
as_written: That proposal is controversial
source: Cooper et al., Science 2021; critical responses in the literature

text: About 565 million years ago the field was about ten times weaker than today, the weakest known
as_written: about ten times weaker than the field you have today
source: Bono et al., Nature Geoscience 2019

text: The Ediacaran biota and the following Cambrian explosion are when complex animals first appear
as_written: the first large, complex animals appear
source: Narbonne 2005, Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences

text: Bono et al. linked the recovery of the field to inner core nucleation, but the age of the inner core is disputed
as_written: When exactly the inner core began is itself disputed
source: Bono et al., Nature Geoscience 2019; Zhou et al., Nature Communications 2022

text: Earth's dynamo was already running at least 3.45 billion years ago
as_written: at least three point four five billion years ago
source: Tarduno et al., Science 2010
